pr_title: [ENHANCEMENT] Alerts: remove metrics for removed Alertmanagers
pr_body:
So they don't continue to report stale values.

Fixes #6864
pr_comments:
For the general context (see also #6864): The traditional orthodox view would be that a program should avoid changing the metrics it exposes over its runtime. However, for programs with higher complexity, we have routinely deregistered or deleted metrics that aren't used anymore. If you partition metrics by backend, and your backends have high churn, you can accumulate a lot of "dead" metrics. I think in the current state of affairs, it is fine to delete those metrics.

What do you all think?

The code changed here is ancient, BTW. Let's page old-hands like @juliusv and @roidelapluie , but anyone else, please chime in if you have an opinion.
I see. Thank you for the updated PR. I guess it will work now. But adding a test would be better, of course.
I think this one can be merged.
@bboreham Gonna leave it up to you to do the final merge, just because it's been sitting here for a while and I want to make sure you're still happy with it all as well.

issue_context.title: Stale metrics for prometheus_notifications_sent_total
issue_context.body:
**What did you do?**
If prometheus was connected to one alertmanager and successfully sent alerts, but after that the addresses of alertmanagers have changed (new kubernetes have been rolled out), then in the metrics `prometheus_notifications_.*` there will be metrics on old alertmanager.  Is it possible to remove metrics from unused alertmanager when reloading prometheus?

**What did you expect to see?**
When we re-create pods with new addresses, we want old alertmanager metrics to disappear from prometheus. 

**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**
Prometheus continues to give metrics about old alertmanager's: http://joxi.ru/GrqqgplHk8dYnr?d=1
Because of the dependent metrics, we can't now understand if there are alertmanagers we use that we can't send the metrics through.

**Environment**

* System information:
```
Linux 5.3.0-28-generic x86_64
```

* Prometheus version:
```
prometheus, version 2.16.0 (branch: HEAD, revision: b90be6f32a33c03163d700e1452b54454ddce0ec)
  build user:       root@0fdd9501c22e
  build date:       20200220-10:44:36
  go version:       go1.13.8
```

* Alertmanager configuration file:
```
alerting:
  alertmanagers:
  - kubernetes_sd_configs:
    - role: endpoints
      namespaces:
        names:
        - monitoring
    scheme: http
    path_prefix: /
    timeout: 10s
    api_version: v1
    relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_service_name]
      separator: ;
      regex: madison-proxy
      replacement: $1
      action: keep
    - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_container_port_number]
      separator: ;
      regex: "80"
      replacement: $1
      action: keep
```
comments: Counters don't become invalid due to the thing they refer to no longer existing, using the erors metrics should catch this.

Hello from the bug scrub.

Revisiting this, we have to say that traditionally, it's a good practice that a binary never removes any metrics that it has once exposed. A counter that isn't moving anymore can just stay around. It's rate will be zero, and that's how you can see that nothing is happening there anymore.

Having said that, it has become quite common for more complex programs with several subsystems that come and go, to remove metrics related to a certain instance of a subsystem once that instance is deleted. So this could also be done for Alertmangers to avoid cluttering the metrics of a Prometheus servers with more and more AM's if the latter have a high churn. @bboreham has drafted a PR how to do this. Let's see what reviewers think.

review_comments: shouldn't we drop `latency` metrics as well?
Sure, do you have a list?
I think all the related per-AM metrics are defined here https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/594b317ecca7f619f308589fefce836aa5bd7d7d/notifier/notifier.go#L143-L168
